name: Gniewko Oak

location.address: Lesnictwo Rudak forest section 178n, Brzoza, Gmina Wielka Nieszawka
location.neighbourhood: Brzoza, Gmina Wielka Nieszawka, near Torun

access: Free; stands in state forest (Lasy Panstwowe, Nadlesnictwo Gniewkowo, Lesnictwo Rudak) open to public foot access under Poland's general right of access to state forest land
transport: No public-transport stop at Brzoza itself; roughly 10km / 20 minutes by car or bike north of Torun city centre
verify_notes: One of a trio of nature monuments designated together on the same forest plot (no. 3178/8, section 178n) by Wielka Nieszawka municipal council resolution XLIII/207/2014 of 7 October 2014, gazetted 31 October 2014: this oak plus two limes, Lipa Bolka (xxx_004) and Lipa Brata Alberta (xxx_005), all within about 15 metres of each other, a genuine walkable trio, one obvious place to stand. Girth CONFLICTS between sources: the forest district's own page (gov.pl/Nadlesnictwo Gniewkowo, citing the council resolution) gives 375cm; Wikidata gives 415cm and adds a height of 26m. Both agree on species, the Oct 2014 designation date and location; flagging the girth discrepancy rather than picking one. No age recorded in either source (Polish registers rarely carry one); left undocumented rather than estimated, since girth alone is a weak basis for oak dating without a source doing the calculation. Wikidata coordinate (52.930759, 18.711634) sits within about 15m of the Commons-geotagged coordinate used here, corroborating the pin. HELD 2026-09-07: this is a 3-tree cluster, below the 4-tree floor, and does not clearly pass the single-famous-tree-destination test (a municipal legal designation and a forest-district webpage, not evidence of a wider tourist destination the way Rogalin is). Kept here fully verified rather than published, in case a Torun page or further evidence of fame opens a container for it.
